description: Composite three-panel figure mixing XRD with TEM/SAED/EDS. (a) Eight vertically stacked XRD patterns (y-axis "Intensity (a.u.)"; x-axis "Diffraction angle 2θ (degree)", 35–80°, 5° ticks) labelled bottom-to-top CR, 600 °C, 700 °C, 800 °C, 900 °C, 950 °C, 1000 °C, 1050 °C, annotated in-panel with colour-coded symbols: "(111) FCC" red, "(110) BCC" blue, "(211) β" olive, "(Cr7C3)" orange, "(111) γ" green. FCC (111) near 43°, (200) near 50°, (220) near 74° and BCC (110) near 44.5° with a weak BCC (200) near 65° occur throughout; olive β markers appear only at 700–900 °C; the BCC peak is strongest at 900 °C; carbide markers are drawn at 950 °C and 1000 °C and none at 1050 °C. (b) TEM of DP950–5: dark particle chain along a grain boundary (point ①), inset magenta Cr EDS map, 200 nm scale bar, plus SAED of "Cr7C3 carbides" indexed (1̄100), (011̄0), (101̄0) at B = [0001]. (c) TEM of DP1000–5: 1 µm overview with points ② (Ferrite SAED, (1̄32), (13̄2), (200), B = [023]) and ③ (Austenite + κ-carbides SAED, (11̄1)γ, (200)γ, (1̄1̄1)γ and (01̄1)κ, (100)κ, B = [011]); a 20 nm inset resolves intragranular κ-carbide nanoparticles, printed r: 0.86 ± 0.20 nm, f: 1.56 %.

subfigures.description: Stacked XRD patterns (Intensity (a.u.) vs Diffraction angle 2θ, 35–80°) for eight conditions: CR, 600, 700, 800, 900, 950, 1000 and 1050 °C. Colour-coded diamond markers with in-panel annotations '(111) FCC' (red), '(110) BCC' (blue), '(211) β' (olive), '(Cr7C3)' (orange) and '(111) γ' (green) track FCC, BCC, β-Mn and carbide reflections; β markers appear only at 700–900 °C, BCC peaks are visually strongest at 900 °C, and carbide markers appear at 950–1000 °C and are absent at 1050 °C.

TEM analysis of DP950–5: a bright-field image showing a chain of dark particles decorating a grain boundary (marked ①, red circle/arrow) with an inset magenta Cr elemental map showing a Cr-rich elongated band along the same boundary; 200 nm scale bar. The accompanying SAED pattern is labelled 'Cr7C3 carbides' and indexes (1̄100), (011̄0) and (101̄0) with a red dashed rhombus at zone axis B = [0001].

TEM analysis of DP1000–5 in four sub-images: a 1 µm bright-field overview with green circles ② and ③ and red connecting lines; a SAED labelled 'Ferrite' for ② indexed (1̄32), (13̄2) and (200) at B = [023]; a 20 nm high-magnification image showing ultrafine dark intragranular κ-carbide nanoparticles with printed red text r: 0.86 ± 0.20 nm and f: 1.56 %; and a SAED labelled 'Austenite + κ-carbides' for ③ indexed (11̄1)γ, (200)γ, (1̄1̄1)γ (red) and (01̄1)κ, (100)κ (blue dashed) at B = [011].

observations.observation: Panel (a) contains eight stacked XRD patterns whose right-hand labels, read bottom to top, are CR, 600 °C, 700 °C, 800 °C, 900 °C, 950 °C, 1000 °C and 1050 °C.
Panel (a) x-axis is labelled 'Diffraction angle 2θ (degree)' and spans 35–80° with 5° ticks; the y-axis is labelled 'Intensity (a.u.)' with no absolute scale.
In panel (a) the CR pattern shows strong FCC (111) and (200) peaks with a weaker BCC (110) peak, and carries no β-Mn or carbide markers.
Olive diamond markers annotated '(211) β' are drawn only on the 700 °C, 800 °C and 900 °C patterns of panel (a).
In panel (a) the BCC (110) reflection is visually the most intense in the 900 °C pattern compared with the other annealing temperatures.

In panel (a) markers associated with the orange '(Cr7C3)' and green '(111) γ' annotations appear on the 950 °C and 1000 °C patterns, while only red FCC and blue BCC markers are drawn on the 1050 °C pattern.
The caption states that Cr7C3 carbides were identified in DP950–5 (panel b) and intragranular κ-carbide nanoparticles were identified in DP1000–5 (panel c).
The caption states the structures were formed by annealing the cold-rolled steel at 600–1050 °C for 5 min and were examined by XRD (a) and TEM (b, c).
The citing text states that β-Mn phase was found at 700–900 °C and that annealing at 900 °C for 5 min gave clearly the strongest BCC diffraction peaks among all annealings.

The citing text states that κ-carbides and Cr7C3 carbides both appeared at 950–1000 °C but disappeared at 1050 °C, and that κ-carbide formation consumes Mn/Al/C atoms, reducing the austenite lattice parameter and shifting its peaks to higher 2θ.
The citing text states that the measured ferrite fraction is largest at 900 °C and decreases above 900 °C, suggesting ferrite-to-austenite transformation.

Panel (b) is a TEM image of DP950–5 (scale bar 200 nm) showing a chain of dark nanometre-scale particles along a grain boundary marked ①, with an inset Cr elemental map rendered in magenta showing a Cr-rich elongated band at the same boundary.
The panel (b) SAED pattern is labelled 'Cr7C3 carbides' and indexes (1̄100), (011̄0) and (101̄0) inside a red dashed rhombus at beam direction B = [0001].

In panel (c) the ② SAED pattern is labelled 'Ferrite' and indexes (1̄32), (13̄2) and (200) at B = [023], while the ③ SAED labelled 'Austenite + κ-carbides' indexes (11̄1)γ, (200)γ, (1̄1̄1)γ in red and (01̄1)κ, (100)κ in blue dashed outline at B = [011].
The 20 nm scale-bar image in panel (c) shows ultrafine dark κ-carbide nanoparticles dispersed within the matrix and prints the values r: 0.86 ± 0.20 nm and f: 1.56 %.

unreadable_items: panel (a): exact symbol-to-phase correspondence in the in-panel legend is ambiguous where markers overlap (green '(111) γ' versus olive '(211) β' diamonds sit near each other at low 2θ)
panel (a): no absolute intensity scale or peak-position values are printed, so peaks can only be located relative to the 5° gridlines
panel (b): the Cr EDS map inset carries no scale bar or colour-scale units of its own
